title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper, introducing the main concept and focus area of the research.

extractions.description: The paper conducts a broad empirical study on the effects of reducing batch size in deep reinforcement learning (RL). It finds that smaller batch sizes lead to performance benefits and reduced computational costs across various agents and architectures, contrary to the common practice of using larger batch sizes. The study highlights the importance of batch size in online RL and provides an analysis of the learning dynamics influenced by batch size choices.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper is focused on empirical analysis of batch sizes in reinforcement learning, without a direct link to climate change.
climate_change_is_central.quote: In this work we conduct a broad empirical study of batch size in online value-based deep reinforcement learning. We uncover the surprising finding that reducing the batch size seems to provide substantial performance benefits and computational savings.

primary_category.justification: There is no direct reference to any climate change-related themes or categories in the paper. The research is primarily about optimizing deep reinforcement learning algorithms.
primary_category.quote: Surprisingly, to the best of our knowledge there have been no studies exploring the impact of the choice of batch size in deep RL.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not address any climate change sub-categories, as it is primarily an empirical study on reinforcement learning methodologies.
primary_sub_category.quote: One of the central concerns for deep reinforcement learning (RL) is how to efficiently make the most use of the collected data for policy improvement.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper is focused on reinforcement learning techniques and does not cover climate change aspects.
new_primary_category.quote: The aim is to learn a policy πθ : S 7→ A parameterized by P∞ θ such that the sum of discounted returns Eπθ [ t=1 γ t rt ] is maximized; here, the state-action trajectory (s0 , a0 , s1 , a1 , . . .) is obtained by sampling an action at ∼ πθ (· | st ) and reaching state st+1 ∼ P (· | st , at ) at each decision step t, and rt ∼ R (· | st , at ).

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The focus is not on climate change but on technical optimization of RL systems.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: In value-based methods, the policy is obtained as the argmax of a learned Q-function: πθ (s) ≡ arg maxa∈A Qθ (s, a).
